title: Resolve streaming stop-sequence inversion during multi-variant failover in Dedicated pools
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Customer reported intermittent over-generation and truncated eval outputs for streaming calls immediately after Dedicated pool autoscale events. Behavior surfaces only when a hosted->dedicated routing fallthrough occurs (routing chooses a warmed variant, then fails over to a newly-provisioned instance) and for requests with explicit per-customer stop sequences set. Root cause hypothesis: the streaming chunk flush optimization bypasses the per-request stop-sequence check on the first chunk emitted by the fallback model, and stop-sequence precedence is inverted when the routing layer synthesizes a continuation response. Impact is dataset/eval noise and some production features returning unexpected trailing tokens for a subset of customer prompts.
reproduction_steps:
1) Configure customer-specific stop_sequence header (e.g., ["
", "END"]) on Hosted route with dedicated fallback enabled
2) Send a streaming generate request with a prompt that exercises early-stop (short expected output) while triggering Dedicated pool cold-start by saturating pool capacity

3) Observe successful partial streaming chunks from warmed variant, then failover to newly provisioned dedicated instance and continued streaming without honoring stop_sequence on the first resumed chunk
4) Validate with internal e2e harness reproducer (infra/streaming-failover-repro) to confirm deterministic reproduction under test harness
root_cause_analysis: Routing layer creates a continuation context when a request is forwarded between variants; previously we relied on the non-streaming finalizer path to apply stop-sequence filters

An optimization that short-circuits stop-sequence checking for first-chunk flush (introduced in runtime-1.22 to reduce latency) assumes finalizer semantics and does not run for resumed streaming continuations

When continuation context is built during failover, the per-request stop sequence is attached but filter ordering is inverted: continuation stream emits chunk before filter executes, causing over-generation
This only affects dedicated failover/resume flows and streaming endpoints; non-streaming and hosted-only flows are unaffected
work_done: Instrumented routing layer to log continuation context metadata (routing:continuation:meta) and added metrics for resume_count and stopseq_mismatch (metrics dashboard: console->Serving->Failover)
Implemented upstream fix: ensure stop-sequence filter runs before any chunk flush on resumed streaming contexts (patch: runtime/streaming/continuation_stopseq_gate)
Added unit + integration tests covering: single-chunk resume, multi-chunk resume, and customer-specific stop-sequence precedence
remaining_tasks: Backport fix to runtime-1.24 branch and cut release candidate
Coordinate canary rollout across Dedicated clusters in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 (SRE runbook updated)
Notify affected customers and include recommended mitigation (temp: disable dedicated failover or add explicit trailing stop token to prompts)
Run 48h canary and monitor stopseq_mismatch and customer-uptime metrics before full rollout
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Fix touches streaming hot path and could regress latency micro-optimizations. Mitigation: added microbenchmarks and latency gates in CI; performance delta must be <2ms P95 to pass
Risk: Backport may diverge if branch has different streaming refactor. Mitigation: coordinated with branch owner (ENG-branch-runtime-1.24) and will create a small compatibility shim if needed
